comment: Budget of a capability rebuilt as a template against the implementation it replaced (#279): its run time and its median peak heap over the reference's, per input. Run time is judged by Student's t interval at `confidence` over rounds (separate processes of the bench), each giving its median paired ratio; it decides only after the round counts in `looks`, each at `confidence`, so an input's verdict is wrong with at most their summed error; an input whose interval straddles its ceiling is measured in further rounds up to the last look, and fails if still undecided (#293). Inputs whose reference runs faster than floor_ns are judged together, by the sum of their medians, since a run of a few microseconds is mostly timer noise. Small inputs may also exceed their references' summed medians by at most small_slack_ns each, and any input its reference's peak heap by at most slack_bytes: a template's fixed cost of a few microseconds or kibibytes per rule is no regression on a model of a handful of objects.

exceptions.reason: The generated fixture's meshes are 12-triangle boxes, so counting costs nearly nothing and the template's fixed cost per object (a read, its evidence, the range judge) dominates; on every public model it runs within 1.11x.
The generated fixture states none of the case's properties, so every wall is a finding worded through the template's messages; on every public model it runs within 1.03x.
